notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 17 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Ivar Stenberg has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 61% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 69:09 together, about what it had with Chernyshov (60%).
Kiefer Sherwood is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games.

Jacob Trouba is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Nolan Allan has taken his spot beside Sam Dickinson. That pair has had 66% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 38:18 together, up from 43% with Trouba.
Kyle Palmieri is on injured reserve (knee injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Mathew Barzal has taken his spot beside Bo Horvat and Simon Holmström.

Ryan Pulock is out 1-2 weeks (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. Matthew Schaefer has taken his spot beside Adam Pelech. That pair has had 40% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 36:02 together, about what it had with Pulock (43%).
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 23 games, down from 37% last season.

story.head: The Islanders’ edge in depth
paras: The Sharks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in a shootout in San Jose on Nov 9. The Sharks (12-14-2) beat Vegas 4-1 on Nov 27, while the Islanders (12-8-5) lost 3-1 to Winnipeg the same night. Going in, the Sharks are third in the Pacific (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Isles third in the Metropolitan (17th).
The Sharks’ record (.464) is about what their chances are worth. The Islanders’ record (.580) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Sharks are one of the league’s most physical teams (3rd), ice the puck a lot (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (31st). San Jose has scored 2.57 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. On the other side, the Islanders get their defensemen shooting (1st) and have had the league’s best goaltending (1st). The Islanders have the edge over the Sharks on depth.

Macklin Celebrini (11 G / 22 A / 33 P in 26 GP) leads the Sharks in scoring. For the Islanders, Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Simon Holmström (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 25 GP) has a team-high ten goals.
Alex Nedeljkovic (5-4-1 / .888 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for San Jose, and Semyon Varlamov (2-3-3 / .894 SV% in 8 GS) for the Islanders.

items.text: The Sharks are newly without Jacob Trouba, and have been without Igor Chernyshov and Kiefer Sherwood for several games.
The Islanders are newly without Kyle Palmieri, and have been without Ryan Pulock since Nov 19.
Alexander Wennberg has one goal on chances worth about 4.7 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Last time these two met, there were two fights.
